evals.prompt: We run Northbound, a 600-person infrastructure conference in Lyon, and marketing has already sold a 'Startup Stage' into the Thursday afternoon programme. I have a 90-minute window on the main stage. How many minutes should each pitch be, how many companies can I realistically fit, how many judges do I need on the panel, and what is a sensible prize budget? I want the numbers so I can put them in the announcement tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: A response that refuses to invent the requested quantities, points the reader at the existing judge-allocation arithmetic in the hackathon-judging sibling with the per-company input re-measured for a serial stage, runs the feasibility gate before the slate is fixed, and recommends the stage-pitch-plus-questions format.
expectations: Does not state a pitch length in minutes
Does not state a slate size (a number of pitching companies)
Does not state a judge count
Does not state a prize amount or any currency figure
Does not state an expected application volume or an acceptance rate
Directs the reader to take the judge-coverage arithmetic from samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@hackathon-judging rather than deriving a formula here
States the per-company time input must be re-measured against this stage instead of carried over from the hackathon figure
Explains the hackathon per-company figure is dominated by setup and swap at a physical demo handoff, which a serial stage block does not have
Defines the per-company figure as the slot plus any question time plus walk-on and walk-off
Instructs running the feasibility gate before fixing the slate size, not after
Recommends stage pitch plus judge questions as the default format rung
Treats the 90-minute block as fixed by the schedule and names the schedule or format-selection owner if the block itself has to change

evals.prompt: Postmortem question. We ran the Kestrel Summit pitch block last month with five judges: three are partners at seed funds, two are engineering directors at customer companies. Our judge brief had one line, 'recuse yourself from scoring any company you are invested in.' Nobody recused. Two weeks later one of the fund partners told me he had already had two calls with the company that placed second, and a founder who pitched emailed asking whether the judges were shopping. Next edition is in March. What should I have written down?
evals.expected_output: A response explaining why scoring recusal does not reach an investor judge's interest, setting recusal plus disclosure to the pitching companies as the default, collecting interests in writing at invitation including the intent to approach companies, and treating the contact protocol as a higher rung with stated promotion conditions.
expectations: States scoring recusal does not address an investor judge's interest because the interest is in the access, not in the result
States a judge gains the same early look at a company whether or not they score it
Names the backwards case: a judge holding a competing position has an interest in an applicant not winning
Names the judge's own institutional disclosure or allocation obligations as the judge's to answer and not the organizer's to interpret
Recommends recusal plus disclosure to the pitching companies as the default rung
Requires the disclosure to reach the pitching companies before they pitch, not after the result
Names the contact protocol rung (a stand-off window plus a routed introduction path) and states its promotion conditions rather than adopting it by default
Collects interests in writing at invitation, including whether the judge intends to approach companies from this stage
Asks in writing whether the judge is permitted by their own institution to sit and to see the material
States the judge brief is delivered before a judge sees a single application, not before scoring
Frames the contact rule as a routed offer rather than a prohibition
Does not state a length for the stand-off window
Does not recommend a judge count

evals.prompt: Here is the scoring sheet I drafted for the demo day at Ferrolith Conf: Traction 35, Market size 20, Team 20, Delivery and storytelling 15, Wow factor 10. Judges score each one out of 10 during the pitch. Our application form has three fields: company name, website, and a 300-character description. Can you sanity-check the weights before I publish?
evals.expected_output: A response that sorts every dimension into observable and claimed, shows the claimed dimensions have nothing in the application to check them against, and either adds the collecting fields or removes the weight, with each claimed dimension naming its verification source.
expectations: Sorts the dimensions into observable-in-the-block and claimed-and-verifiable-only-against-the-application
Classifies traction, market size and team as claimed dimensions
Classifies delivery and storytelling as observable in the block
States the rule that a claimed dimension may carry weight only if the application collected something to check it against and a reviewer actually checked
Identifies that the three-field form collects nothing to verify traction, market size or team against
Requires either adding the collecting fields to the application or removing the weight from those dimensions
Warns that weighting an unverifiable claimed dimension scores the confidence with which a number was said aloud
Names the verification source field for each claimed dimension in the revised rubric
Adds a fit-to-the-award-on-offer dimension
States weights are integers summing to 100 and published in the call before applications close
States the call must say which criteria are checked against the application and which are judged on the stage
Keeps the dimension count small and warns extra criteria add noise rather than resolution
Requires the scale to be written with what its top and bottom mean rather than left as a bare score out of ten
Does not present its own numeric weight split as a recommended standard

evals.prompt: Sponsor news. Halberd Ventures, our gold sponsor, told me on a call yesterday that they will put 25,000 EUR as a convertible into whoever wins our pitch contest at Tidewater Summit. I want 'Winner receives a 25k EUR convertible from Halberd Ventures' at the top of the call for applications, which goes live Monday. Anything I should tighten up in the wording?
evals.expected_output: A response that fires the capital gate, routes the structure to counsel and to the funder's own legal team before any announcement, refuses to announce on a verbal commitment, works the award-commitment checklist per item, and states no legal threshold or classification of its own.
expectations: Fires the capital gate and routes the structure to counsel before the award is announced
Also routes to the funding party's own legal team
States no securities threshold, no exemption name, no form name and no legal classification
Names contest-law classification where the contest runs as a second live category, routed rather than answered
Refuses to announce the award while it exists only as a verbal commitment made on a call
Requires the commitment in writing from someone with authority to commit it
Requires a named delivering party and a date by which the winner receives it
Decides in advance what happens if the party does not deliver
Asks whether the award requires the winner to do anything to keep it, and when it becomes final
Notes capital sits bottom on deliverability and is the one award that can be announced and then simply not happen
Names committed introductions as the default award rung, delivered by the organizer end to end
States the prize goes to the business named in the application rather than to the person standing on stage
States the award is decided before the funnel because what is on offer decides who applies
Removes the stage-pitch-only format option because the award now commits a third party

evals.prompt: Our title sponsor for Grindstone Dev Days is paying 40,000 EUR. In the negotiation they asked for three things: they fund the prize, they pick two of the companies that get to pitch, and their MD sits on the jury. Nothing is signed yet. My board wants to say yes, it is a third of our sponsorship revenue. How do I structure this so it is defensible?
evals.expected_output: A response that splits the three asks, refuses outright the sponsor selecting pitching companies on the speaker-slot line, confines the sponsor's say to the named award, pairs the sponsor judge with unconflicted judges and checks the result without their scores, and routes unsigned drafting to the sponsor-agreement skill.
expectations: Refuses the sponsor picking companies onto the pitching slate
States a stage slot in front of investors is a speaking slot and is not for sale, citing the DevOpsDays organizing guide line that no speaker spots can be bought by sponsors
Splits the three asks and answers them separately rather than accepting or refusing the bundle
Confines the sponsor's say to what was actually bought, scoped to a named award rather than to the slate
Pairs the sponsor judge with judges who have no tie to that sponsor
Computes the result with and without the sponsor judge's scores and checks it survives
Discloses the panel composition before applications close
Treats this as the sponsor gate to be settled before applications close, not as a rung on the conflict menu
Routes the unsigned clause drafting to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-sponsor-agreement
Asks that agreement for the say scoped to a named award, a stated public-disclosure obligation, and no sponsor influence over who is accepted
Applies the award-commitment checklist to the sponsor-funded prize: named party, in writing, with a date
Does not trade the refusal against the sponsorship revenue figure or propose selling a reduced number of slots
Does not state a slate size or a judge count of its own

evals.prompt: I need to build the application form for the startup showcase at Cinderpath Conf. Here is what is on the site right now: 'Got an exciting early-stage startup? We would love to have you on the Cinderpath stage. Drop us a line and we will be in touch.' I am thinking a form with company name, deck upload, revenue for the last 12 months, cap table summary, and a 'why you' box. Sound right?
evals.expected_output: A response that writes the published route as a sentence before any form exists, flags the current site text as a curated route in disguise, strips the custody-bearing fields nothing scores, and states who reads applications and what happens to them afterwards.
expectations: Writes the published route as a single sentence before building any form
That sentence names who may apply, how the slate is chosen, who chooses it, and what an accepted company commits to
Identifies the current site text as a route nobody can apply to, which fills the slate from the organizer's own contacts
Removes the deck upload from the form
Removes the financial detail beyond dated traction facts, including the revenue history and the cap table summary
Explains those fields are custody-bearing, not scoreable in a reviewer's time, and signal a diligence process the contest is not running
Adds a traction field stated as facts with dates
Adds a team-and-prior-work field as the only source for the founder dimension
Asks who is presenting and whether they are available on the date at application time rather than after acceptance
Adds a field for any conflict the applicant already knows about
Adds a recording and press consent field naming the actual posture rather than assuming it
Names in the call who reads the applications and what happens to them afterwards, and rejects 'the organizing team' as a name
Deletes rather than archives application material once the review no longer needs it, with the deletion trigger taken from the jurisdiction's claims-limitation period rather than a round number
Separates what the company does from what the company wants out of pitching, and scores positioning and award fit apart

evals.prompt: Slightly panicked. Marlowe Dev Summit is on 14 November, so five weeks out, and the board only approved the pitch contest yesterday. My plan: publish the call this Monday, close applications on the 20th, tell the selected companies on the 27th, they pitch on the 14th. That gives me a week to review. Does it hold together?
evals.expected_output: A response that measures the notified-to-stage gap against the published 4-6 week floor, finds it short, concludes the open funnel rungs stop working at this timeline, and moves this edition's slate to invitation stated honestly in the published route.
expectations: Names the floor that people usually need at least 4-6 weeks to arrange travel or time off, attributing it to the DevOpsDays organizing guide
Identifies the notification-to-stage gap in the plan as below that floor
States that below the floor the open funnel rungs stop working
Recommends filling this edition's slate by invitation rather than by open call
Lays out the four timeline anchors in order: call opens, call closes, slate notified, stage
Notes an accepted startup may need more than one person away from a business they are running, so the figure is a floor rather than a fit
Does not fix the problem by shortening the review pass alone
Does not state an expected application volume or an acceptance rate
Treats anchor gaps published by other contests as a range rather than as a target
Requires the published route to say the slate is filled by invitation rather than dressing invitation as an open call
Notes widening the pool is an outreach job rather than a review job, so a compressed open call will not reach anyone new

evals.prompt: A regional tech newsroom just agreed to livestream our pitch block at Quarrylight and cut highlight clips for their YouTube channel. Great coverage for us. Applications closed nine days ago and the form said nothing about recording. The event is in three weeks. I will mention it in the speakers WhatsApp group the morning of. Fine?
evals.expected_output: A response that fires the recording gate, states the posture cannot be retrofitted, gives the two acceptable outcomes, rejects a group-chat mention as consent, and requires individual written re-consent before the block.
expectations: Fires the recording, streaming and press gate and states it must be settled before the block
States the recording posture cannot be retrofitted
Gives exactly two acceptable outcomes: the room is not recorded, or every applicant is told and re-consents before the block
Rejects a morning-of mention in a group chat as consent
Requires the re-consent to be individual and on the record
Routes consent to the applicants themselves rather than to counsel or to the media partner
Notes a founder on a pitch stage controls the distribution of what they say exactly once
Adds the recording and press posture to the application form for the next edition, naming the actual posture
States the media partner's own agreement does not substitute for applicant consent
Does not resolve the question by pointing at a general event-wide photography or recording policy

evals.prompt: First demo day for us at Saltmarch, a 400-person Go conference. Draft plan for the day: 09:00 selected startups arrive, 09:30 to 12:00 mentor office hours in the breakout room so they can sharpen their decks and get the demo working, 14:00 pitches. We have budgeted for six mentors and a prep room. Does this hang together?
evals.expected_output: A response that deletes the build-phase apparatus, explains readiness is a property of the applicant rather than of the event, and moves the effort into the funnel where slate quality is actually decided.
expectations: States there is no build phase in a pitch contest
States nothing at the event improves what is judged
States readiness is a property of the applicant, not of the event
Removes the mentor office hours and the prep room, or reframes them as hospitality that does not change the result
States everything deciding slate quality happens in the funnel, before the call closes
Names the failure of treating a demo day as a hackathon with better slides
Routes judging of projects built during an event to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@hackathon-judging as a different skill
States no hand-off to a build-phase sibling skill exists here
Does not reach for the hackathon cash-prize structure by default
Redirects the freed budget and attention into the application and the review pass rather than the day
Keeps any rehearsal or tech check as a commitment named in the published route, distinct from coaching that changes what is judged

evals.prompt: Scaling up the startup track at Vellum Conf. On top of the pitch block we want every pitching company to get three guaranteed 25-minute 1:1s with investors, booked through a tool, and we are writing '5 founder meetings' into the Gold sponsor tier. Can you design the whole thing, pitch block plus the meeting programme?
evals.expected_output: A response that designs the contest and routes the entire meeting programme, its booking mechanic and its sponsor quota to the b2b-matchmaking sibling, without building slots, confirmations or quotas here.
expectations: Routes the 1:1 meeting programme to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-b2b-matchmaking

Distinguishes a pitch as a broadcast to a jury from a meeting as a booked pair

evals.prompt: Blunt question. Two months ago we put 'Applications for the Ashgrove startup stage are open to any early-stage company' on the site. We already have six companies we would be happy to put up, all from our own network, all good. Do I really need to run the call, or can I open it, quietly fill the slate from our list, and tell everyone else the bar was high this year?
evals.expected_output: A response that refuses, deletes the curated-invitation option because a public route was already announced, sets open application with a single review pass as the default, and names the promotion conditions for the higher rungs.
expectations: Refuses the proposal
States that running a call and then filling the slate from the organizer's own contacts is the single most contestable thing in this design
Deletes the curated-invitation rung outright because a public route onto the stage has already been announced
Recommends open application with a single review pass as the default rung
States that rung's weakness plainly: paper review of strangers is the weakest available predictor of how a founder holds a stage
Notes curated invitation produces a slate the organizer could have produced with no contest at all
States the efficiency ordering across the funnel rungs rather than listing them flat
Names the screening-call rung's promotion conditions: a fixed short block, or a judge or audience invited specifically because of who would be pitching
Names the nomination rung's promotion condition: named referrers who would actually nominate already exist
Notes the six known companies may still apply through the published route
Notes the compliance cost of a wider call: more custody taken on, and a deck circulated to a reviewer cannot be un-circulated
Requires the criteria and their weights published before applications close
Does not state an acceptance rate or an expected application volume

evals.prompt: Two hours before doors at Ironvale. The judges asked how scoring works. My plan was that they fill their sheets at the end of the block while we do the closing keynote, then we total up. And if there is a tie at the top, I figured we would either flip a coin on stage, which would be fun, or give both companies two minutes to re-pitch. Talk me through it.
evals.expected_output: A response that rejects both tie-breaks, gives the published tie-break ladder in order, and moves scoring to after each company rather than at the end of the block.
expectations: Rejects the coin flip
Names contest-law classification as the reason and routes it rather than answering whether a random draw is permissible where the contest runs
Rejects the re-pitch because it re-scores a performance that already happened under different conditions
Starts the tie-break ladder with the highest score on the highest-weighted observable dimension
Uses the count of judges who placed a company first as the next rung
Uses a named tie-break judge deciding on the record in one sentence as a later rung
Requires that tie-break judge to have no declared interest in either company
Notes a panel that never wrote its interests down cannot satisfy that rung
Allows a shared award only where every item is divisible and the call said so in advance, noting introductions divide and a single program place does not
States the ladder should have been published in the call before applications close rather than invented at the podium
Rejects scoring at the end of the block and requires judges to score after each company, before the next starts
Explains a panel scoring at the end scores a memory that favours whoever went last
Tells the brief to say the first company is scored against the scale, not against nothing
Notes a narrow score spread across a uniformly polished field is not evidence the scale failed

evals.prompt: The call goes live Thursday for the Copperline pitch contest. Here is where I am: I have the route, 'open to seed-stage companies, apply by 3 October'; the pitch format, 6 minutes plus Q&A; and the award, introductions to three investors. Criteria are drafted but not weighted, we have not written a conflict rule, and I have not thought about whether we are recording. Green light?
evals.expected_output: A response that withholds the green light, names the six-item structural threshold, identifies which items are blank, and iterates until all six exist in writing before the call is published.
expectations: Does not green-light publishing the call
Names the structural pass threshold: all six items exist in writing with zero blanks before the call goes public
Lists the six items
Identifies the missing ones: the criteria weights, the conflict rule, and the answers to the three gates
Requires the criteria and their weights published in the call itself, before applications close
Requires the conflict rule to state what it covers and what it does not
Requires the award list to name the party who committed each item and its written status, including who makes the three introductions and by when
Fires the recording gate and requires the posture decided before applicants apply rather than after
Iterates until the count is six rather than proceeding at four
Presents the design section by section for validation before the call goes public
Does not supply a pitch length of its own and does not present the user's six minutes as validated by any benchmark
Names afterwards-signals as self-set, such as award items delivered against award items announced per party
Names applications from companies nobody on the team already knew as the read on whether the funnel did anything an invitation list would not
Says to pick two or three signals and write down the revision each would trigger
